title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
read_level: full (arXiv HTML; the HTML served is v1 although metadata lists v2; v2 not separately read)
metadata_mismatch: title/authors match; metadata version is v2, HTML read is v1 (03 Nov 2026)
why_wsp: Proposes an LLM editor (GPT-6 Astra vs Qwen3-VL) that inspects U-Net code, weights, activations and sampling previews and proposes restricted bias/filter/skip edits accepted by no-reference IQA feedback; executed experiments use numerical search on small networks, not an LLM.
domain: image super-resolution / diffusion restoration (ResShift, SinSR, SUPIR); color calibration
editor: proposed: GPT-6 Astra (primary), Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct (comparison); executed experiments: seeded numerical search (no LLM)
target: proposed: ResShift, SinSR, SUPIR U-Nets (sizes not given); executed: small residual nets with 4,611, 6,147 and 4,867 parameters
interface: code/tensor tools (declared update operations: bias shift, high-frequency filter change, skip-projection rescale)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (1,020 candidate trials, accept/rollback on NR-IQA feedback)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: limit: 'limiting accepted changes to three layers and fewer than 0.1% of model parameters' (Abstract); executed: 'These changes correspond to 0.0651% of parameters in the pixel model and 0.0488% in the patch model.' (Sec 7.3); SR demo 'changes three scalars, or 0.0616% of the model' (Sec 7.4)

headline_results.claim: Tables 2-5 report LLM-editor diffusion numbers (e.g. GPT-6 Astra on ResShift dMANIQA 0.041, 72% preference vs CMA-ES 58%); their execution status is unclear: paper says executed studies 'do not test an LLM editor or a diffusion model' and full studies 'are needed'
headline_results.quote: The full diffusion and human studies are needed to determine whether an LLM editor can deliver the intended perceptual improvement.

headline_results.claim: Executed color calibration: patch model uniform-shift color-prior distance 0.984 -> 0.422
headline_results.quote: Under the uniform shift, the patch model reduces color-prior distance from 0.984 to 0.422.

headline_results.claim: Proxy failure: nominal condition gets worse on test despite lower feedback loss
headline_results.quote: In the nominal condition, the patch model increases color-prior distance from 0.188 to 0.423 and increases clipping.
mean luminance-gradient energy increases by 3.56%, while the maximum change in chromatic differences remains below 3×10^-7

cost.claim: Projected denoiser steps for 1,020 trials (not executed)
cost.quote: 1,020 valid candidates and one baseline require 980,160 denoiser steps at 15 sampling steps, or 3,267,200 at 50 steps.

baselines_and_controls: Protocol: random search, coordinate search, CMA-ES, statistics-based editor, source-only/summary-only interfaces, matched-norm random directions, budget ablations. Executed experiments: original weights only.
runs_and_variance: Protocol specifies five sessions per LLM editor and scene-level bootstrap; executed experiments are single seeded searches per condition; no variance reported.
robustness_of_edits: Executed: test on 28 held-out images; feedback improvement did not generalize in nominal/spatial conditions. No fine-tuning/quantization tests.
verification: none formal; save-and-reload check: 'Fresh inference agrees with the cached prediction within 2×10^-6' (Sec 7.3)
limitations_stated: Calibration study 'does not establish useful U-Net layer localization, an LLM advantage, or improved human preference for diffusion SR'; 'The experiment did not execute 1,020 full diffusion runs or collect standard learned NR-IQA scores'; restricting layers does not eliminate global side effects; feedback overfitting.
code_or_data: none found (uses public CBSD68 via FFDNet repo)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of weight-space programming [16]
notes_for_survey: Mostly a protocol paper: LLM-editor diffusion results in Tables 2-5 are not described as executed, while executed experiments use numerical search on few-thousand-parameter nets. Executed part documents a reference-free feedback proxy improving while held-out performance worsens.
